script: "Swim test disaster: 1 in 5 kids fails, but that's not the worst part...". So, I am at this summer camp, and we have these super strict rules, right? Like, if you want to swim in the main pool, you got to take this swimming test, and if you pass, you get to use all three areas: the main pool, the splash pad, and the shallow pool. But if you don't pass, you're stuck in the splash pad and shallow pool only. (I know, right?) So, we all took the test, and a few kids didn't pass, which, I get it, it's okay. But this one mom is literally insane – she's all upset because her kid didn't pass, and she's telling all the other parents to tell their kids to stay out of the main pool too. Like, what, are we all supposed to feel bad for her kid or something? I am listening to her, and I am thinking, "Girl, your child didn't pass the test, it's not the end of the world." But then, one of the other parents pipes up, and she's all, "Or you could teach him how to swim, since you had the same complaint last year." Honestly, I died, like, laughing, and I am thinking, "Yaaas, queen, you go!" (literally insane). So, the mom tries to give this whole speech about how her kid is feeling sad and left out, and the other mom is just like, "Uh, maybe if you taught your kid to swim, they wouldn't be so sad next year?" (I am shook). Anyway, that's my story – a bunch of entitled mom drama at summer camp. The mom got shut down, and I got a good laugh out of it.
